clue.text: Students turn up with beer

indicators.note: to turn something here is to flip the following word so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager

explanation.surface: Students arrive at the party bringing beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' flips UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are learners at a school, a direct synonym for students.

clue.text: Peppers detective with remembrances — leave me out of it!

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: leave, with out of it, tells us to remove letters from the word
completing the instruction: these letters go out of the word

parts.note: mementos are keepsakes or remembrances

explanation.surface: A detective, bothered by mementoes, begs to be left out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave me out of it' removes ME from MEMENTOS, leaving MENTOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimentos are sweet red capsicums, the kind stuffed into olives.

clue.text: Fail to promote festival?

definitions.meaning: to pass someone over is to skip them for promotion
the Jewish spring festival marking the Exodus from Egypt

explanation.surface: A worker wonders if being denied promotion is cause for celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means skip over someone; as one it is the Jewish feast.

clue.text: Substantial recall of most integral components

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards
most, with components, means most of the word's letters are taken
the parts of the word that remain once its start is gone

explanation.surface: Something weighty brings to mind most of its essential parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most integral components' gives EGRAL, five of INTEGRAL's eight letters; 'recall of' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and substantial are synonyms for something of considerable size.

clue.text: Mysterious secretion giving off nitrogen is unstable

indicators.note: letters that are unstable fall apart and settle in a new order
giving off means letting something go, so a letter leaves the word secretion

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a puzzling discharge that releases nitrogen is volatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving off' removes N from SECRETION, leaving SECRETIO, which 'is unstable' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something esoteric is obscure, understood only by a select few, so it seems mysterious.

clue.text: Outstanding giveaway in Hong Kong, perhaps

indicators.note: the giveaway word goes in the region's abbreviation

parts.note: Hong Kong is an example of a SAR, a Special Administrative Region of China
a tell is an unconscious sign that gives a poker player away

explanation.surface: A free gift handed out in Hong Kong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giveaway' looks like a free gift but is a poker tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar performance means excellent, star quality, so outstanding.

clue.text: Twitter enthusiast to stop daughter running away with musician

parts.note: Donald Trump was famous for prolific posting on Twitter

indicators.note: the daughter's letter runs away, leaving the word

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or stop

explanation.surface: A social-media addict tries to stop his daughter eloping with a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running away' drops D from DETER, leaving ETER. 'Twitter' suggests birdsong, apt for a trumpeter swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter plays the trumpet, so is a type of musician.

clue.text: Starting to redecorate, so long for wireless devices

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, so long

explanation.surface: Begin redecorating and bid farewell to old wireless sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless is the old British word for a radio set.

clue.text: One who's concerned about English occupation

indicators.note: the carer goes about, around, the letter for English

parts.note: a carer is someone who cares, who is concerned

explanation.surface: Someone worried about an English job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CARER around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is someone's profession or line of work, synonymous with an occupation.

clue.text: Island insects swarm cross goats

indicators.note: insects that swarm crowd around something, enclosing it

parts.note: bees are flying insects
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: On an island, swarming insects bother some bad-tempered goats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarm' puts BEES around X.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats with large curved horns.

clue.text: Cheapskate with no tip for meal, sorry!

parts.note: a miser is a stingy person, a cheapskate

indicators.note: having no tip means losing the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A diner apologises for being too mean to leave a tip after the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no tip for' takes the T off TABLE, leaving ABLE. 'Tip' looks like a gratuity but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry in the sense of wretched or pitiful, as in a sorry state, matches miserable.

clue.text: Huddersfield displays dairy production equipment

indicators.note: the town name displays, or shows within it, a run of its own letters

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town shows off its dairy machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: Huddersfield is a town in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's udder is where milk is produced, humorously described as equipment for dairy production.

clue.text: Necktie quickly sent back by Earl

indicators.note: sending a word back means reading it from the end to the start

parts.note: soon means shortly or quickly

explanation.surface: A necktie is returned in a hurry by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses SOON to NOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's rope is grimly called a necktie, a joking slang synonym.

clue.text: Chromosomes cut with stone instrument

parts.note: X and Y are the sex chromosomes, paired in males
to lop is to cut off branches
a hone is a whetstone for sharpening blades

explanation.surface: A lab scene: chromosomes are sliced with a stone tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Troublesome orange leader: emperor of America

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
US is short for United States of America

explanation.surface: A jab at an orange-tinted American leader styled as a troublesome emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and heavy, so it is troublesome.

clue.text: Sharp by the smell of it

definitions.meaning: exactly, precisely on time or target, as in at six sharp
wine tasters judge aroma, the nose, so this is how a wine smells

explanation.surface: Something pungent, judging by its odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely right, and literally refers to a wine's aroma.

clue.text: Ceremony is just caught

indicators.note: something caught by the ear is heard, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: right means fair or just

explanation.surface: A legal remark: a ceremony is fair only when someone is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' means heard: RIGHT and RITE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Fake illness a gremlin concocted

indicators.note: concocted letters are mixed together into something new

explanation.surface: A mischievous gremlin invents a sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be sick to avoid work.

clue.text: Borders of Paraguay disrupt serene mountain range

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer letters
disrupted letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Paraguay's frontier troubles shatter a peaceful mountain scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupt' rearranges SERENE to RENEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the range between France and Spain.

clue.text: Infection starts off seeming trivial, yet escalates

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words are taken off them

explanation.surface: A medical warning: an infection that looks minor can grow worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small bacterial infection of an eyelid gland.

clue.text: Nurse finally learnt about the intestines?

definitions.note: the noun phrase defines an adjective; the question mark flags that it means relating to the gut

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word
about signals the letters are turned about, scrambled

explanation.surface: A nurse has at last learned about the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learnt about' reads as studied, but 'about' is the anagram signal working on learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral means relating to or via the gut, as in enteral feeding by tube.

clue.text: Appropriately ignoring the Spanish state

indicators.note: ignoring some letters leaves them out of the word

parts.note: germanely means relevantly or appropriately
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A diplomat's quip about duly overlooking the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops EL from GERMANELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany is a European nation, an example of a state.

clue.text: Butcher's good and pointy implement

parts.note: a lance is a long pointed spear

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop sells good, sharp knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: a butcher's is a look, a quick peek.

clue.text: Harsh treatment regimen given orally

indicators.note: given by mouth, spoken, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: a course is a series of medical treatments

explanation.surface: A tough drug programme is taken by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given orally' looks medical but signals the sound: COURSE sounds like COARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough or crude in texture or manner, hence harsh.

clue.text: Rascals swindle prosperous outsiders

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rogues cheat rich outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous people, rascals.

clue.text: Actors fool around with her in part of theatre

indicators.note: letters fooling around are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Actors mess about with an actress in a section of the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra is the area in front of the stage, or the stalls seating in American usage.

clue.text: Father has hotel within the county

indicators.note: the hotel letter sits within the word for father

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dad keeps a hotel in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts H inside SIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire is a British county, as in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Criticise all the candidates

definitions.meaning: a list of candidates standing for election

explanation.surface: Pour scorn on every person standing for election.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to attack harshly, and a list of nominees for office.

clue.text: A young lover is more befuddled by love

indicators.note: a befuddled word is confused, its letters muddled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A youthful suitor grows more confused by love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' rearranges MORE to ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Montague youth who loves Juliet; his name now stands for any ardent young suitor.

clue.text: Figure skater's last elegant performance bags 100

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is used
bags means holds inside, so the hundred sits within
a performance of the letters puts them through a new routine

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A figure skater's final graceful routine scores 100.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges ELEGANT to ETANGLE; 'bags' puts C inside it as ECTANGLE. 'Figure' looks like part of 'Figure skater' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a geometric shape, a four-sided plane figure with right angles.

clue.text: Extremely lazy after third day of wind

indicators.note: the outer letters come after the festival in the answer

parts.note: Easter Sunday is the third day counting from Good Friday, when the resurrection is said to have come

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Something very idle comes after the third day of a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a breeze that blows from the east.

clue.text: King hates fancy red suit

indicators.note: fancy letters are elaborated, rearranged into a new form

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch dislikes an elaborate scarlet outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges R with HATES. 'Suit' looks like clothing but is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the four suits in playing cards, two are red; this one shows heart symbols.
